chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: Arrangers from inside the band versus outsiders
summary: Stanley Dance asks why outside arrangers are hired; Greene does not know the money.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, it seems to me that people -- musicians in the band write some of the best arrangements for the band. Like Frank Wess had that 'Segue in C'
-- and 'Everyday' and that one you still play even nowatimes. Very good.

I never could understand why when you go to make an album they get one of these outside guys to do it, because they -- you know I've wondered -- they must have to pay -- I would have thought they'd have to pay them more than if -- I mean, they paid paid or Eric Dixon to do it.
Do you know the answer to that? No?
I don't know what the salaries are. I mean, as far as that's concerned -- only Basie can answer that. I don't know.

Willard Alexander, But, it seems to me that if you say to a guy like this Nestice. or any of them -- you say -- "I want ten arrangements for a record session in a month's time" -- you get two good ones and eight
Whereas if you gave the work out to four different arrangers --
Mm hmm. Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
-- arrangers -- yeah. And, it will be a variety of things.
I mean, you ought to listen to those albums they've made in the last few years. They're good, in a way --
-- but yet, they're not very distinctive.
